To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
positively charged blockers bind to the open state of a pentameric liganded gated ion channel and the location of two binding sites for inhibitors that differ in size.

we solved the structure of a bacterial pentameric liganded gated ion channel in the open state, which revealed a binding site for large blockers in the middle of the channel and another for smaller blockers at the intracellular end.
the open pore of GLIC can accommodate two positively charged molecules, one in the narrowest part of the pore, and one in the wider part of the pore.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, function, and pharmacology of the pentamergic ligand gated ion channels (pLGICs).
the molecular mechanisms of ligand binding, activation and inhibition in the family of pentameric liganded gated ion channels.
understanding the molecular basis of ion channel function, in particular, ligand gated ion channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structure provides a structural foundation for the understanding of the interaction of the channel with a wide range of blockers that is relevant for understanding the entire family of pentameric lig and gated ion channels.
the structural basis for open state channel inhibition in GLIC is the same as in Cys-loop receptors.
the structural basis of the block of the prokaryotic GLIC channel is the same as that of the eukaryotic homologs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the binding of positively charges molecules to the open channel is a two-step process, with the initial binding occurring at the narrow intracellular end and the second step being at the center of the pore.
the binding sites of the inhibitors are located at two distinct regions of the channel, one in the narrow intracellular entry to the pore and the other in the center of transmembrane pore.
we have identified the binding site for two different classes of blockers, the divalent metal ions and the larger organic blockers such as TBPB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a large cavity in the center of GLIC and that this cavity is lined by aromatic amino acids that can interact with a large number of different molecules.

the mechanism for channel block in the prokaryotic homolog GLIC is fundamentally similar to that of the more complex eukaryotic pentamers, with the same two binding regions, but that there are important differences in how the binding regions are used to achieve block.
there are two distinct binding sites for positively charged blockers of the pentamergic ligand gated ion channels.
